title: "Joint distributions"

Recipient length and theme length are measured on the same dative token. Separate distributions discard that pairing. A **joint distribution** assigns mass to the ordered length pair and thus preserves which values co-occur.

## Definition

Let $R$ be recipient length in words and $T$ be theme length in words. Their joint PMF is

$$
p_{R,T}(r,t)
=\mathbb{P}(R=r,T=t).
$$

It must satisfy

$$
p_{R,T}(r,t)\geq0,
\qquad
\sum_r\sum_t p_{R,T}(r,t)=1.
$$

For any set $A$ of length pairs,

$$
\mathbb{P}\big(\langle R,T\rangle\in A\big)
=\sum_{\langle r,t\rangle\in A}p_{R,T}(r,t).
$$

For absolutely continuous variables, the corresponding definition is

$$
\mathbb{P}\big(\langle R,T\rangle\in A\big)
=\iint_A f_{R,T}(r,t)\,\mathrm dr\,\mathrm dt,
$$

where $f_{R,T}(r,t)\geq0$ and
$\iint_{\mathbb R^2}f_{R,T}(r,t)\,\mathrm dr\,\mathrm dt=1$.

## The observed dative joint PMF

We return to the [English dative table introduced on the Poisson page](poisson-distribution.qmd). The original study treats relative length as one of many predictors of dative realization; here we first describe the paired constituent lengths without fitting that response model.

```{r}
#| label: dative-joint-pmf
library(ggplot2)

dative <- read.csv(
  "data/english-dative/dative-alternation.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  na.strings = c("", "NA")
)
joint <- as.data.frame(table(
  recipient_length_words = dative$recipient_length_words,
  theme_length_words = dative$theme_length_words
), responseName = "count")
joint$recipient_length_words <- as.integer(as.character(joint$recipient_length_words))
joint$theme_length_words <- as.integer(as.character(joint$theme_length_words))
joint <- subset(joint, count > 0)
joint$probability <- joint$count / nrow(dative)

modal_cell <- joint[which.max(joint$count), ]
event_probability <- sum(joint$probability[
  joint$recipient_length_words <= median(dative$recipient_length_words) &
  joint$theme_length_words <= median(dative$theme_length_words)
])

stopifnot(
  nrow(dative) == 3263L,
  abs(sum(joint$probability) - 1) < 1e-12,
  all(joint$probability >= 0) # dqr-allow: scale-boundary
)

modal_cell
event_probability
```

The most frequent observed pair is a recipient of `r modal_cell$recipient_length_words` word(s) with a theme of `r modal_cell$theme_length_words` word(s). Its empirical joint mass is `r sprintf("%.3f", modal_cell$probability)`. Both values belong to the same token; independently tabulating the two variables would lose that fact.

```{r}
#| label: plot-dative-joint
#| fig-cap: "Observed joint distribution of recipient and theme lengths. Point area represents the number of dative tokens in each length pair."
ggplot(joint, aes(theme_length_words, recipient_length_words, size = count)) +
  geom_point(color = "grey30", alpha = 0.65) + # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
  scale_size_area(max_size = 7) +
  labs(x = "Theme length (words)", y = "Recipient length (words)",
       size = "Token count") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

The dense lower-left region shows that both constituents are often short, while the rarer points retain the long tails. A joint PMF describes this pinned table; repeated verbs and speakers still limit independent-sampling claims.

## Check your understanding

1. Compute the empirical probability that both lengths are at most their empirical medians.
2. Verify one joint cell directly from the row-level data.
3. Explain why shuffling theme lengths leaves both marginal PMFs unchanged but changes the joint PMF.
4. Which identifier would you preserve when asking how the pairing varies by verb?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. For recipient length $R$ and theme length $T$, the empirical probability that both are at most their respective medians is 0.425375. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. The modal joint cell contains 572 rows with recipient length 1 and theme length 2, giving $572/3263=0.175299$. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. Shuffling theme lengths preserves every recipient and theme count separately but breaks the row pairings that determine the joint PMF. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. The `verb` identifier should be retained to study how recipient–theme length pairings vary across repeated verb types. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->

</details>

The [next page](marginal-distributions.qmd) recovers either one-variable distribution by summing the joint mass.
